name: Darcy Reyes
life: “I still remember winning a certificate nobody at home knew was mine.” On Wednesday, near the corner by Juniper Tailor, Darcy looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I asked the school to use my own nickname on the shortlist. I know how it feels to win under someone else's name.
appearance: Darcy is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose. Usually dressed in a brown corduroy jacket with a narrow brass watch set a little fast, Darcy squares up pieces of paper while thinking when listening.
personality: Darcy thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Darcy sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To enter the shortlist under the chosen name.
family: Rowan Kelly is Darcy’s older cousin. Darcy puts the kettle on. Rowan chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Winter afloat*, Rowan says, “I budgeted for timber and forgot the cost of a bed.”
connections: Cory Walker. One former applicant's embarrassment helps a new candidate choose a preferred name.
